# SF Ballot Atlas

A static, nonpartisan comparison of San Francisco voter guides for the November 3, 2026 general election. Reference images informed the layout only. No endorsement values were transcribed from them.

Vite + React + strict TypeScript keep filtering, comparisons, and quiz scoring entirely in the browser. Python and BeautifulSoup collect the build-time snapshot. There is no backend or runtime scraping. Fonts are bundled locally, with their licenses.

## Run

Requires Node 22.12+ and Python 3.10+.

```sh
cd sf-voter-guides
npm ci
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r scraper/requirements.txt
npm run dev
```

Vite prints the preview URL. The checked-in snapshot is sufficient to run and build; scraping is optional during setup.

```sh
npm run scrape
npm run validate
npm test
npm run test:scraper
npm run build
npx playwright install chrome
npm run test:e2e
```

`npm run scrape` reuses cached responses. To fetch fresh responses, run `npm run scrape -- --refresh`. The GitHub runner starts without a raw-response cache and therefore collects live data each day. Raw responses are gitignored under `cache/`; parsed facts, provenance, derived metrics, changes, and review reports live in `data/`.

## Initial coverage

Collected from live sites on October 23, 2026:

- 17 guides, 61 contests, and 1,037 explicitly represented cells.
- 616 substantive recommendations; 11 explicit no-position statements; 410 cells where no recommendation was found.
- 206 cells parsed directly from eight guides: GrowSF, SPUR, League of Women Voters SF, SF Democrats, Harvey Milk Club, SF Bay Guardian, SF Tenants Union, and DSA SF.
- 421 low-confidence cells contain aggregator-only recommendations. They are marked with an asterisk in the matrix and listed individually in `data/REVIEW.md`.
- The 61 contests include 13 judicial retention questions, represented as Yes / No measures. House District 15 is excluded because it is outside San Francisco.

Coverage is incomplete. Candidate lists contain names discovered in endorsements and are not verified complete ballot rosters. Aggregator multi-name cells do not establish ranking order. Multi-seat slates are unordered sets. DSA candidate cells capture its formal endorsements; additional strategic recommendations may appear in its prose. Rationales remain null unless supplied by a sourced manual override; the scraper does not infer arguments from advocacy prose.

The aggregator exposes server-rendered HTML tables, so Playwright is unnecessary for scraping. The six specifically requested primary guides were all accessed at their own sites. SF Democrats links to a separate election-specific page; the scraper follows it. DSA's main domain works; an initially discovered `live.dsasf.org` URL had a certificate mismatch and was not used. No certificate checks were disabled.

YIMBY Action's linked election page returns 404. Labor Council's robots endpoint returns a redirect response that the client cannot resolve, so its direct site is skipped. Alice B. Toklas's linked page covers earlier elections; Abundance's page does not identify this election. Their aggregator records remain low confidence. Other inspected pages without dedicated parsers also use low-confidence aggregator records. No paywalls were bypassed and no PDF or image endorsements were guessed.

The aggregator's `robots.txt` returns HTML rather than valid robots directives. Other robots policies are checked before fetching pages; denials and unavailable policies stop direct collection. Requests use an identifying User-Agent, a one-second minimum interval, applicable crawl delays, HTTP timeouts, and an on-disk response cache. Source failures appear in the review report and the Methodology view.

## Data and corrections

`data/dataset.json` contains guides, contests, positions, allowed topics, source-access notes, and the error-report link. `data/derived.json` contains build-time contest split scores, guide-pair agreement, and camp agreement. Every cell has a source URL, retrieval timestamp, confidence, and collection method. `source_url` identifies the actual evidence: an original guide page for direct cells, or SF Endorsements for aggregator-only cells. A guide's own URL is separately recorded on its guide entry.

`npm run build` validates the snapshot before compiling. Validation rejects absent citations, unknown IDs, duplicate or omitted cells, invalid stances or candidate IDs, invalid topics, missing timestamps, and guides with no substantive positions.

Edit `data/manual_overrides.json` to correct a cell. Overrides take precedence on every scrape. Use discovered guide, contest, and candidate IDs. Each override needs a reason and its own supporting citation. Example:

```json
[
  {
    "guide_id": "growsf",
    "contest_id": "sf-prop-d",
    "stance": "yes",
    "source_url": "https://growsf.org/voter-guide/san-francisco-voter-guide-november-2026-election/#prop-d",
    "retrieved_at": "2026-10-23T19:00:00Z",
    "confidence": "high",
    "reason": "Reviewed the explicit Yes on Proposition D heading."
  }
]
```

Measure stances: `yes`, `no`, `no_position`, `no_recommendation_found`. Race stances: `candidate:<candidate-id>` or `ranked:["candidate-id-1","candidate-id-2"]`, plus the two absence states. For multi-name cells, `selection_type` distinguishes `ranked`, `unordered slate`, and `order unverified`. Do not call a slate a ranked ballot.

To add a guide, add a row in `scraper/config.json` with ID, display name, editorial camp, exact aggregator name, primary URL, and type. Add a direct parser when the source has a stable structure. If the aggregator does not contain the guide, a direct parser must supply substantive positions or validation fails. Keep the topic vocabulary and report-error URL in this config. Then scrape, inspect `data/REVIEW.md`, run checks, and review the source citations.

## Metrics

For a measure, split = the minority's Yes / No count divided by all Yes / No positions. Missing cells and explicit no-position statements are excluded. Bucket boundaries use exact values: Most split ≥40%; Contested ≥20% and <40%; Mostly agreed <20%.

For a race, count each guide once per endorsed candidate. The leader has the most guide endorsements. Split = the share of guides that support none of the tied leaders. Slates that include a leader count as supporting that leader. All-candidate ties can produce 0% despite different selections; cells show the actual sets. This candidate-based rule can differ from treating each slate as a distinct choice.

Pairwise agreement requires identical positions on shared substantive contests. Unverified candidate order is ignored; verified rankings must match in order. Camp agreement pools within-camp guide pairs weighted by shared contest count. Camps are editorial groupings, not confirmed self-descriptions or a measure of ideological distance.

Quiz rankings compare only overlapping Yes / No answers and always show the denominator. Answers stay in component memory. Filters, sorting, hidden rows/columns, and guide selections are encoded in the URL. Quiz answers enter the URL only after the user enables sharing. A shared answer URL is readable by anyone receiving it. No analytics or browser storage are used. URL referrers are suppressed by the production headers.

## Daily review workflow

The monorepo root contains `.github/workflows/sf-voter-guides-refresh.yml`. It runs daily at 14:23 UTC through November 3, 2026, using the San Francisco calendar date. Later scheduled jobs exit without scraping. It builds a fresh snapshot, runs validation and unit tests, and opens or updates `codex/sf-voter-guide-data` as a review PR. It never merges or deploys automatically.

`data/changes.json` records changed stances; the PR body lists every change. `data/REVIEW.md` lists all low-confidence and missing cells, direct-versus-aggregator differences, source failures, and drops in guide coverage. Inspect these before merging. The initial snapshot has no previous production baseline.

GitHub Actions must be enabled, and repository Actions settings must permit GitHub Actions to create pull requests. The check workflow also runs the browser tests. Workflows become active after these files reach the repository's default branch. They have not been executed remotely as part of local development.
